summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted due to dizziness, nausea, leg weakness, and imbalance, initially concerning for stroke. She was last known well at 10:00 a.m. on the day of admission. Evaluation revealed no acute stroke on CT or MRI of the brain. Her symptoms were attributed to peripheral vestibulopathy, likely triggered by metabolic disturbances including hyperkalemia (K+ 6.4). She underwent four hemodialysis sessions during admission, with improvement in electrolyte levels and symptom resolution. She experienced an episode of hypotension during one dialysis session, which resolved with fluid administration and machine recalibration. Meclizine was prescribed for persistent dizziness, and outpatient physical therapy was arranged for balance training. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications, including increased omeprazole and amlodipine, and instructions to continue dialysis and follow up with neurology and hematology.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Other and unspecified nonspecific immunological findings
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
